acceptanceCriteria: Repository heavy targets (make test/gate/dogfood-change/dogfood-check and the lane test wrapper) run their child processes below interactive scheduling priority (nice 10 or more) by default, with an opt-out variable.

Under a reproduced lane load of at least 3 concurrent package test runs on a 12-core host, 50 consecutive Claude Code user-prompt adapter invocations finish under the 2 s hook limit with no dogfood-event-deadline fallback; timings retained as evidence.
If priority alone does not meet that bound, the adapter's user-prompt path is profiled under load and its remaining load-sensitive work (git probes, snapshot reads) is moved off the synchronous path.
body: 2026-10-22: every UserPromptSubmit hook in the orchestrator session fell back with dogfood-event-deadline while three lanes ran tests (load average 41, rising from 15; 12 cores). Measured at load 25-29 with the installed build 712: `corvint adapter claude-code user-prompt` takes 0.39-0.45 s on this session's enrolled path and 0.41-0.88 s unenrolled, so the hook is fast at idle and fails only when CPU-bound test children starve it of CPU against its fixed 2 s timeout (hooks.json timeout 2). Earlier fixes (V1-0881, V1-1120, V1-1422) cut adapter work but the failure recurs whenever lane load passes about 40. Local mitigation applied the same day: /private/tmp/cem10-build/heavy.sh now runs its command under `nice -n 15` (verified: child nice 15). The repository's own heavy make targets still run at normal priority. Related: V1-1627, V1-1628 (host throttle/semaphore), V1-1496 (fallback cause reporting).
title: Hook adapters still hit dogfood-event-deadline when lane test load starves them of CPU; heavy targets must run below interactive priority
